title: Semi-magic dihedral squares
summary: Let $Γ$ be a group of order $n^2$ and $SMS_Γ(n)=(a_{i,j})_{n\times n}$ be an $n\times n$ array whose entries are all distinct elements of $Γ$. If there exists an element $μ\inΓ$ such that for every row $i$, there exists an ordering of elements such that $$ a_{i,j_1} a_{i,j_2} \dots a_{i,j_{n-1}} a_{i,j_n} = μ $$ and for every column $j$ there exists an ordering of elements such that $$ a_{i_1,j} a_{i_2,j} \dots a_{i_{m-1},j} a_{i_m,j} = μ, $$ then $SMS_Γ(n)$ is called a \emph{$Γ$-semi-magic square of side $n$} and $μ$ is called a \emph{magic constant}.
